title: HonoStar Production Readiness and DX Tracker
description: Standalone execution tracker for the major production-readiness and developer-experience work required to move HonoStar from a strong alpha toward a production-ready framework. This file is intended to be the single source of truth for the work plan and should be kept current as slices move.
goals: Make framework checks reproducible on a clean clone without relying on prebuilt artifacts.
Guarantee or explicitly model reliable event delivery for the server-authoritative CQRS model.
Establish release, test, CI, and support policies required for external production use.
Reduce authoring friction by making core APIs more typed, less stringly, and more opinionated.
nonGoals: Rewriting the core hypermedia + SSE architecture away from server authority.
Adding client-owned state management or optimistic-sync-first design.
Broadening the public API surface before the golden path is stabilized.

tracerSlices.title: Make Typecheck and Codegen Hermetic
tracerSlices.description: Ensure demo/starter typecheck, prepare, and build flows work from a clean checkout without depending on stale or prebuilt package dist output.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: A framework cannot be considered production-ready if its own validation pipeline is not reproducible in a fresh environment. Current app typechecking depends on build artifacts existing first.
problemsObserved: apps/demo and apps/starter run `honostar prepare` before typecheck, but preparation imports Node helpers from built package output.
Workspace validation breaks on clean clones when package dist files are missing.
Consumers will hit brittle setup behavior and stale-artifact bugs.
implementationPlan: Decouple `honostar prepare` from compiled workspace package output.
Use source-based imports, TS project references, or an internal codegen entrypoint that works before package build.
Make `pnpm typecheck` pass on a clean clone without a prior `pnpm build`.
Document the invariant in build docs.
acceptanceCriteria: `git clean -xfd && pnpm install && pnpm typecheck` succeeds.
`pnpm --filter honostar-demo typecheck` succeeds without prebuilding `@honostar/core`.
No app-level scripts require stale dist files to exist.
risks: May require package export changes or internal source entrypoints.
Can expose hidden circular dependencies in the codegen path.

tracerSlices.title: Add Durable Event Publication
tracerSlices.description: Introduce a reliable event publication mechanism so shared-state mutations and CQRS event fanout cannot silently diverge after database commit.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: The framework's core promise is server-authoritative shared truth. If state changes commit but events fail to publish, connected clients drift from canonical state and recovery becomes ad hoc.
problemsObserved: `FxResponder.publish()` and `publishTo()` push directly to the bus after mutation.
Redis/NATS bus publish failures are logged but not retried or made transactional.
There is no outbox, durable log, or commit boundary tying state mutation to event emission.
implementationPlan: Choose an explicit reliability model: outbox pattern, durable log, or retryable publish contract.
Add first-class framework support for mutation plus event publication, not app-specific glue.
Make failure semantics visible to apps and tests.
Provide migration guidance for existing command handlers.
acceptanceCriteria: Framework has a documented reliable publication story for production usage.
Mutation handlers can opt into durable publication through a first-class API.
Tests cover publish failure, retry/replay, and no-lost-event scenarios.
risks: Cross-runtime abstractions may be harder once persistence is introduced.
The API should avoid forcing a single ORM or database choice.

tracerSlices.title: Define and Test Failure Semantics for the Bus Layer
tracerSlices.description: Make pubsub error behavior explicit, testable, and observable across Memory, Redis, NATS, and Cloudflare adapters.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Even with durable publication, production users need clear semantics for backpressure, dropped connections, publish errors, retained patch behavior, and reconnect recovery.
problemsObserved: Publish failures are mostly logged and swallowed.
Retention semantics differ by adapter and are only partially documented.
Operational behavior under disconnection or slow consumers is not exposed as a framework contract.
implementationPlan: Document expected guarantees per adapter.
Add explicit hooks, metrics, or callback surfaces for publish and reconnect failures.
Standardize retained-patch behavior and limits where possible.
Expand tests around disconnects, adapter failures, and self-heal behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Each bus adapter has documented guarantees and limits.
Publish and subscription failure behavior is covered by tests.
Apps can observe critical bus failures instead of only console logging.
risks: Guarantee mismatches between in-memory and distributed adapters may require capability flags.

tracerSlices.title: Establish CI and Release Gates
tracerSlices.description: Add repository CI, required checks, and release-quality gating for lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, and app smoke coverage.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Without CI, the framework's quality bar only exists locally. Production-ready frameworks need repeatable enforcement on every change.
problemsObserved: No repository CI workflow was found.
No enforced gate exists for cross-workspace validation.
No release workflow or publish policy is present.
implementationPlan: Add CI workflow covering install, lint, typecheck, unit tests, and build.
Run demo and starter smoke checks in CI.
Define release gates and branch protection expectations.
Document contributor expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: Every PR runs CI successfully before merge.
Release workflow documents or automates publish steps.
Broken validation on a clean environment is caught in CI.
risks: CI can initially reveal pre-existing flakiness that must be burned down.

tracerSlices.title: Add E2E and Multi-Tab Coverage
tracerSlices.description: Create browser-level test coverage for full hypermedia workflows, SSE updates, reconnect recovery, and distributed update behavior.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: The hard parts of this framework are browser/runtime interactions, not isolated helpers. Unit tests are necessary but insufficient.
problemsObserved: Core unit coverage is decent, but the demo app has no real tests.
No browser E2E suite was found for navigation, forms, modals, or SSE reconnect behavior.
No multi-tab or cross-instance smoke tests are present.
implementationPlan: Add Playwright or equivalent browser runner.
Cover create issue, label creation, status change, comment posting, auth fallback, modal flows, and reconnect self-heal.
Add at least one multi-tab test proving shared updates arrive and self-heal correctly.
Add one Redis or NATS integration path in CI or nightly builds.
acceptanceCriteria: Demo app has automated browser tests for core framework promises.
At least one reconnect/self-heal scenario is verified in CI.
At least one multi-tab shared-state scenario is verified automatically.
risks: Browser tests can be flaky until dev server startup and test isolation are standardized.

tracerSlices.title: Publish a Runtime Capability Matrix and Support Policy
tracerSlices.description: Turn runtime-agnostic claims into a concrete support matrix with tested capabilities, limitations, and adapter ownership.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Production consumers need to know which runtimes are officially supported, which are experimental, and what features degrade in each environment.
problemsObserved: The framework claims broad runtime support, but the tested and documented support boundaries are unclear.
Cloudflare has its own package, but there is no visible capability matrix.
Operational tradeoffs by runtime are not centralized.
implementationPlan: Define support tiers for Node, Bun, Cloudflare, Deno, and other targets.
Document feature support by runtime: SSE, compression, streaming, retained patches, codegen, asset pipeline.
Align docs and marketing claims with actual support.
acceptanceCriteria: Support matrix exists in docs and is linked from the main README.
Unsupported or experimental combinations are clearly marked.
Adapter-specific limitations are easy to discover.
risks: May require narrowing some current claims rather than expanding implementation.

tracerSlices.title: Ship a One-Call App Bootstrap
tracerSlices.description: Replace most manual middleware and route/SSE wiring with a first-class `createHonostarApp()` or equivalent bootstrapping API.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Both starter and demo require a lot of ordered setup boilerplate. This increases setup mistakes, weakens discoverability, and makes the framework feel lower-level than its pitch.
problemsObserved: App setup requires manual ordering of csrf, renderer, initContext, bus, fxResponder, route collection, and SSE mount.
The SSE route and query collection are easy to forget or misorder.
The golden path is not encoded in a single entrypoint.
implementationPlan: Design a high-level server bootstrap API for the recommended stack.
Let apps opt into defaults while still allowing escape hatches.
Collapse query collection and SSE endpoint setup into the bootstrap flow.
Refactor starter and demo to use the golden path.
acceptanceCriteria: Starter app setup becomes materially smaller and easier to read.
Common framework miswiring is no longer possible on the golden path.
Docs recommend one primary bootstrapping approach.
risks: Need to preserve extensibility without reintroducing too much configuration surface.

tracerSlices.title: Add Typed Datastar JSX Helpers
tracerSlices.description: Introduce typed helpers for common Datastar attribute patterns so app authors stop writing large inline strings and JSON blobs by hand.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: The largest day-to-day authoring pain today is stringly Datastar markup. It weakens autocomplete, syntax predictability, and safe refactors.
problemsObserved: Forms and buttons embed long inline action strings.
Signal initialization often uses raw JSON strings in JSX attributes.
Attribute composition is hard to reuse and easy to break.
implementationPlan: Create ergonomic JSX helpers for `data-on`, `data-signals`, `data-bind`, `data-show`, `data-indicator`, and common network actions.
Prefer typed builder APIs over raw string templates where practical.
Refactor demo hotspots to prove the API reduces noise and improves autocomplete.
acceptanceCriteria: Demo app removes most large inline Datastar strings from core flows.
Common Datastar authoring patterns have typed helper APIs.
Docs present helpers as the preferred authoring model.
risks: Need to avoid a helper layer that becomes more verbose than raw attributes.

tracerSlices.title: Make Dynamic Topics and Query Handlers Typed
tracerSlices.description: Replace regex-heavy dynamic topic handling with typed topic definitions that flow params into query handlers and commands.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Pattern-based topics are currently powerful but awkward. Regex matching and manual `match.groups` parsing reduce readability and correctness.
problemsObserved: Dynamic queries use regex patterns and manual id parsing.
Topic parameter shapes are not inferred into handlers.
Dynamic route params and dynamic topic params feel like separate systems.
implementationPlan: Design typed topic builders or resource topics that encode params structurally.
Flow parsed params into query handlers directly.
Reduce direct regex handling in app code.
Keep contracts and topics aligned so publish/query surfaces share the same model.
acceptanceCriteria: Dynamic query handlers receive typed params, not raw regex matches.
Demo issue-detail topics no longer rely on manual `match.groups` parsing.
Topic definitions and event contracts feel like one cohesive system.
risks: Overdesigning topic builders could make simple string topics harder to use.

tracerSlices.title: Unify Enhanced and Full-Page Action Responses
tracerSlices.description: Provide a first-class action response abstraction so command handlers do not have to branch repeatedly between Datastar and non-Datastar request paths.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: The current ergonomics for progressive enhancement are repetitive and leak transport details into app code.
problemsObserved: Handlers frequently branch on `c.var.isDatastarRequest`.
Validation and success flows duplicate reply-vs-redirect logic.
The enhanced and full-page paths are conceptually one action but are authored as two.
implementationPlan: Add a helper for enhanced-action success/error outcomes with redirect fallback.
Keep the CQRS reply vs publish distinction, but hide transport branching.
Refactor demo commands to use the higher-level action API.
acceptanceCriteria: Demo commands remove most direct `isDatastarRequest` branching.
Validation and redirect behavior remain explicit but not repetitive.
Docs present one canonical way to implement progressive-enhancement-safe actions.
risks: The API must remain flexible enough for apps that need unusual response behavior.

tracerSlices.title: Replace Global Module Augmentation with App-Scoped Typing
tracerSlices.description: Move app variable typing away from global declaration merging toward app-scoped or bootstrap-scoped generics.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Global augmentation works, but it scales poorly across multiple apps, weakens locality, and still encourages escape hatches like non-null assertions.
problemsObserved: Apps extend framework context via ambient module augmentation.
Context typing is less local and less predictable than an app-bound type model.
Demo handlers still rely on non-null assertions after auth middleware.
implementationPlan: Design app-instance-scoped variable typing.
Make the bootstrap or app factory carry the variable shape.
Reduce reliance on ambient declarations in app code.
Tighten auth-aware helper patterns to reduce `!` usage.
acceptanceCriteria: Framework examples no longer require module augmentation for normal usage.
App context typing is local to the app bootstrap.
Demo code removes avoidable non-null assertions tied to context.
risks: A new typing model must not become more complex than the current one for small apps.

tracerSlices.title: Curate and Simplify the Public API Surface
tracerSlices.description: Reduce redundant entrypoints and encode a clearer golden path across page creation, commands, queries, effects, and contracts.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: The framework currently exposes power, but too many near-duplicate choices make it harder to learn and harder to recommend confidently.
problemsObserved: `createPage` and `defineQueryPage` are aliases.
`createHandler` and `defineCommand` are aliases.
Query registration can happen in multiple places.
Contracts publishing has several related entrypoints.
implementationPlan: Define which APIs are primary, which are advanced, and which should be deprecated.
Update docs to emphasize one recommended path.
Optionally add lint rules or codemods for deprecated aliases.
acceptanceCriteria: Docs can explain the golden path without listing many equivalent choices.
Deprecated or advanced APIs are clearly labeled.
New users can follow one obvious route from starter to real app.
risks: Need to avoid breaking existing examples abruptly without migration guidance.

tracerSlices.title: Formalize Release Policy, Versioning, and Adoption Docs
tracerSlices.description: Prepare the framework for real external adoption with release policy, semver expectations, changelog discipline, migration guidance, and production deployment docs.
tracerSlices.whyItMatters: Production readiness is partly technical and partly trust. Consumers need predictable releases, documented breaking-change policy, and deploy guidance.
problemsObserved: Packages are still private and versioned as `0.0.0`.
No release policy or migration path is visible.
Production deployment guidance is fragmented.
implementationPlan: Define pre-release and stable release channels.
Document versioning and breaking-change policy.
Add changelog and upgrade guidance.
Document production deployment prerequisites: secrets, adapter choice, build flow, CI expectations.
acceptanceCriteria: Framework has a documented release policy.
Consumers can discover how to adopt and upgrade safely.
Publishing packages no longer depends on tribal knowledge.
risks: Process work can lag implementation work unless explicitly owned.
